sections.kicker: Prepared for Theory of Ease by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way someone who just found you after the rename would. Here is what stood out.
sections.thesis: Theory of Ease has a lovely line and a product name that pull in two directions.
sections.keep: Your line "For the air you live in." It is short, unexpected, and nobody in skincare owns air yet.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things

pins.quote: For the air you live in.
pins.what: The best line asks the reader to solve a riddle.
pins.why: Without a word on what air does to skin, a new visitor has to guess why this moisturizer is different from Eadem or anyone else.
pins.how: Keep the line, and put one plain sentence next to it about the problem it solves.
pins.label: Your line
pins.cost: People who arrive from Instagram still cannot say what you do after the first screen.

pins.what: The product, the brand and the idea each have a different name.
pins.why: Theory of Ease, Reservoir and the air are three ideas, and a pre launch brand can only teach one at a time.
pins.how: Choose the idea the rest serve, and let the product name prove it.
pins.label: Your names
pins.cost: After a rename, every extra name is one more thing people confuse.

pins.what: The menu already hints at the story you want to tell.
pins.why: A formula and the air as two pages is the start of a point of view a competitor cannot copy.
pins.how: Build the whole front door around that pair, before launch, so Instagram and the site say the same thing.
pins.label: Your structure
pins.cost: Without it, January arrives with a product and no reason to remember it.

sections.intro: You said the messaging across platforms is not landing, and that the rename made things harder. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out.
